servicesIndustries.name: Wholesale Trade
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Wholesale trade output, the demand-side proxy for business investment and merchandise trade flows, declined 1.2% month-over-month and 1.7% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31, the second-weakest monthly print in the services universe behind management of companies.1 Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0434 records this as the steepest year-over-year contraction in any wholesale or retail bucket.1 The dedicated monthly source is the StatCan Wholesale Trade Survey (Table 20-10-0074), which tracks farm product, motor vehicle and parts, and miscellaneous wholesalers.2

The project database carries no NAICS 41 capital tagging because wholesale distribution is a low-capex services sector; sector exposure is tracked through merchandise trade indicators in indicators.json covering agricultural, mineral and forestry exports.3 With the policy rate held at 2.25% following the Bank of Canada's cumulative easing cycle, financing conditions for inventory carry remain looser than a year ago.4

servicesIndustries.name: Retail Trade
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Retail trade output, driven by household consumption and consumer confidence, expanded 0.8% month-over-month and 2.7% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31, one of the firmer services prints in the 20-NAICS table.1 The Statistics Canada Retail Trade Survey (Table 20-10-0008) is the dedicated monthly source for motor vehicle and parts dealers, food and beverage stores, and general merchandise stores.2 The Bank of Canada policy rate at 2.25% defines the household borrowing environment supporting discretionary spending capacity.3

The project database carries no dedicated NAICS 44-45 retail tagging; retail footprint appears within commercial-mixed projects under construction (NAICS 23), which currently total 1,373 projects at $241.8B declared value.4 Population growth from continued immigration and the recent CPI deceleration to 1.8% year-over-year are the demand-side variables tracked in indicators.json for retail sector dynamics.3

servicesIndustries.name: Transportation & Warehousing
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Transportation and warehousing output, sensitive to merchandise trade volumes, fuel costs and business activity, declined 0.7% month-over-month while remaining up 1.6% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1 The fuel input backdrop continues to weigh on operating margins: WTI crude held at $102.77/bbl and natural gas at $2.87/MMBtu, both little changed on the day.2

The project database tracks 601 transportation and warehousing projects at $44.9B declared value, of which 142 are Under Construction and 335 are Proposed.3 The largest items are the Surrey Langley Skytrain BC ($6B, Under Construction), the Trade Diversification Corridors Fund CA ($5B, Proposed), and the Fraser River Tunnel BC ($4.1B, Under Review).3 The Federal Impact Assessment Registry separately tracks three Ports & Logistics items: Wharf 401 Reconstruction at Millerand Harbour QC, the Pathways Alliance CO2 Transportation Network AB, and the Floating Wharf Replacement at Meteghan NS.4

servicesIndustries.name: Information & Cultural Industries
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Information and cultural industries output, driven by technology investment and digital infrastructure capital deployment, expanded 0.9% month-over-month and 3.2% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31, tied with finance and insurance for the strongest year-over-year reading in the services universe.1

The project database tracks 43 information and telecommunications projects totalling $3.0B declared value, of which 11 are Under Construction and 17 are Proposed.2 The largest tagged items are Bell Canada's AI Data Centre at the RM of Sherwood SK ($1.7B construction value, Proposed) and the SaskTel ICT Capital Program SK ($433M, Proposed).2,3 The Wonder Valley AI Data Centre Park Phase 1 in Alberta ($12B, Proposed) cross-references this sector but is tagged under manufacturing in the project database, illustrating the cross-sector reach of AI compute capital expenditure.2

servicesIndustries.name: Finance & Insurance
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Finance and insurance output, the most rate-sensitive of the services sectors, expanded 0.5% month-over-month and 3.2% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31, tied with information and culture for the strongest year-over-year reading in the services universe.1 The Bank of Canada policy rate held at 2.25%, and the listed-equity proxy for the sector — the S&P/TSX Composite — closed at 33,696, up 42.85% year-over-year on a flat weekly print.2,3

The project database carries no direct NAICS 52 capital tagging because financial intermediation, insurance carriers, and the Bank of Canada are non-capex service operations rather than physical-asset sectors.4 Sector activity is tracked through the financial markets block in briefing_latest.json, including the TSX Composite and the BoC overnight rate.2,3 Mortgage origination flows feed back into NAICS 23 residential construction and NAICS 53 real estate, where the project database tracks 157 residential projects at $41.8B declared value.4

servicesIndustries.name: Real Estate & Rental/Leasing
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Real estate and rental and leasing output, driven by mortgage rates, immigration flows and provincial housing policy, declined 0.2% month-over-month while remaining up 1.2% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1 The Bank of Canada policy rate held at 2.25%, defining the marginal mortgage carry environment for residential transactions.2

The project database carries no direct NAICS 53 capital tagging, but the residential subset of NAICS 23 construction overlaps directly with this sector and contains 157 residential projects totalling $41.8B declared value.3 The largest items are the Edmonton Affordable Housing Program AB ($2.6B, Complete) and the PEI Affordable Housing Construction 300+ Units program ($100M, Proposed).3 The BC Government News service reported on March 27 that two completed rental buildings opened in West Vancouver, and the policy tracker links those completions to 51 BC residential projects in the database.4 If mortgage rates ease further, additional residential projects in the Proposed and Under Review queues would advance through zoning and permit phases.

servicesIndustries.name: Professional, Scientific & Technical Services
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Professional, scientific and technical services output, driven by infrastructure project demand and corporate capital budgets, declined 0.1% month-over-month and 0.4% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31, one of the smallest absolute moves in the services universe.1 Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0434 records this as a near-flat reading for engineering, scientific research, and management consulting subsectors collectively.1

The project database carries no direct NAICS 54 capital tagging because professional services are an intermediate input to capital projects rather than a project sponsor.2 The Canada Foundation for Innovation's 92 Research Infrastructure Projects program ($552M, Proposed) is tagged under NAICS 61 educational services in the project database but draws professional engineering and scientific consulting hours.2 Sector activity is most directly cross-referenced to NAICS 23 construction (1,373 projects, $241.8B) and NAICS 22 utilities (1,392 projects, $515.5B), which together represent the upstream demand for engineering, environmental, and technical consulting hours.2

servicesIndustries.name: Management of Companies & Enterprises
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Management of companies and enterprises output, a small and historically volatile services industry concentrated in head-office activity, declined 4.1% month-over-month and 21.9% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31 — the single largest year-over-year contraction in the 20-NAICS table.1 Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0434 identifies NAICS 55 as a concentrated industry where single-period prints have historically fluctuated by double-digit percentages, reflecting the small denominator and corporate restructuring cycles.1

The project database carries no NAICS 55 capital tagging because head-office and corporate enterprise management are non-capex services functions.2 The data quality block in the industry dossier flags this print as historically volatile, and the dossier's anomalies list cites the 21.9% year-over-year decline as a single-period statistical outlier rather than a structural sector trend.1 The Bank of Canada policy rate at 2.25% defines the corporate borrowing environment for enterprise restructuring.3

servicesIndustries.name: Administrative & Waste Management Services
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Administrative and waste management services output, driven by business activity, regulatory compliance demand, and remediation contracts, declined 0.1% month-over-month and 0.2% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1

The project database tracks 17 environment and remediation projects totalling $1.9B declared value, of which 5 are Under Construction and 1 is Proposed.2 The largest items are the Port Lands Flood Protection and Enabling Infrastructure Project ON ($1.3B, Under Construction), the Boat Harbour Remediation Project NS ($367M, Approved), and the City of Regina Railyard Renewal Project SK ($64M, Under Construction).2 These remediation projects sit at the boundary of NAICS 56 administrative services and NAICS 23 construction, with the bulk of declared value running through environmental engineering and waste-management subcontractors.2

servicesIndustries.name: Educational Services
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Educational services output, driven by provincial budgets, K-12 and post-secondary enrolment, and immigration policy, expanded 0.5% month-over-month while declining 1.9% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1 The year-over-year contraction is the largest negative reading in the services education and health bloc.1

The project database tracks 157 education-tagged projects totalling $14.7B declared value, of which 13 are Under Construction and 21 are Proposed.2 The largest items are the Alberta School Construction Accelerator Program — 16 New Projects ($8.6B, Proposed), the Sage Hills University and Residential Community BC ($1.5B, Proposed), and the UBC Medicine 1 Building BC ($567M, Proposed).2,3 The Canada Foundation for Innovation's 92 Research Infrastructure Projects program ($552M, Proposed) is also tagged under this sector.2 If provincial capital budgets confirm the Alberta accelerator program allocation, the proposed school construction queue would advance through procurement and tender phases.

servicesIndustries.name: Health Care & Social Assistance
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Health care and social assistance output, driven by demographics, provincial health budgets, and labour supply in nursing and care occupations, was flat at 0.0% month-over-month while running 2.1% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31, one of the firmer year-over-year prints in the services universe.1

The project database tracks 258 healthcare-tagged projects totalling $20.5B declared value, of which 47 are Under Construction and 39 are Proposed.2 The largest items are the Surrey Hospital BC ($2.9B, Under Construction), the Burnaby Hospital Renewal BC ($2.4B, Under Construction), and the St. Paul's Hospital Replacement BC ($2.3B, Under Construction).2 Hospital capital activity is concentrated in British Columbia, where the three largest items together account for $7.6B of the sector's declared value. Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0022 (SEPH) provides monthly employment-by-industry data for NAICS 62 ambulatory care, hospital, and nursing and residential care subsectors.3

servicesIndustries.name: Arts, Entertainment & Recreation

Arts, entertainment and recreation output, driven by tourism flows, discretionary consumer spending, and immigration-supported population growth, declined 0.1% month-over-month while running 2.2% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1

The project database tracks 150 tourism and culture projects totalling $22.3B declared value, with 94 Under Construction — the highest ratio of Under Construction to total projects in any services sector.2 The largest items are Garibaldi at Squamish Ski Resort BC ($3.5B, Proposed), Union Bay Estates BC ($2B, Proposed), and the Hemlock Valley Mountain Ski Resort Expansion BC ($1.5B, Proposed).2 The British Columbia tourism and recreation pipeline dominates the sector by declared value. Smaller items in active construction include the Mont-Orford National Park Expansion QC ($59M) and the Edmonton Winspear Centre Expansion AB ($33M).2

servicesIndustries.name: Accommodation & Food Services
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Accommodation and food services output, driven by tourism flows, business travel and discretionary household spending, expanded 0.7% month-over-month and 2.3% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1 The agricultural input cost backdrop continued to ease across the soft-commodity complex: sugar futures fell 22.1% year-over-year, coffee fell 19.1% year-over-year, and cocoa fell 60.6% year-over-year.2

The project database carries no direct NAICS 72 capital tagging because hospitality real estate falls under commercial-mixed projects within NAICS 23 construction.3 The NAICS 23 commercial-mixed bucket totals 1,373 projects at $241.8B declared value, with hotel and food service properties forming a subset of that pipeline.3 The sector's strength relative to other services prints is consistent with sustained tourism flows and stable household consumption of food away from home.

servicesIndustries.name: Other Services (except Public Administration)
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Other services output, covering repair and maintenance, personal and laundry services, and religious, grantmaking and civic organizations, expanded 0.2% month-over-month and 0.3% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31 — the smallest absolute movement in the 20-NAICS GDP table.1 The near-flat reading reflects the sector's relatively low cyclical sensitivity, given the essential and recurring nature of repair, personal, and civic services.1

The project database carries no direct NAICS 81 capital tagging because these are small-establishment, low-capex services activities that fall outside the dashboard's $5M-$500M provincial declaration thresholds.2 The Bank of Canada policy rate at 2.25% and headline CPI at 1.8% year-over-year define the household disposable-income environment for personal services consumption.3 Sector employment is tracked through the Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey (Table 14-10-0355) rather than through capital project flows.4

servicesIndustries.name: Public Administration
servicesIndustries.analysis:
Public administration output, driven by government budgets, defence procurement and policy priorities, declined 0.1% month-over-month while running 0.7% year-over-year for the period ending 2026-03-31.1 The sector covers federal, provincial, territorial, local and Indigenous government activity.1

The project database tracks 231 government, defence and Indigenous projects totalling $165.0B declared value — the largest aggregate declared value of any services sector in the database.2 Of those, 40 are Under Construction and 153 are Proposed.2 The three largest proposed items are concentrated in northern and Arctic defence: the Northern Defence and Infrastructure Investment YT ($40B, Proposed), the Arctic Defence and Infrastructure Spending Package NWT ($35B, Proposed), and the Northern Defence Nunavut Military Bases program ($32B, Proposed).2 Defence Construction Canada separately tracks $8B of active infrastructure contracts.3 The Federal Impact Assessment Registry tracks two active Defence items: the DND Relocated Infrastructure Project at the 4th Canadian Division Training Centre ON and the Canadian Coast Guard Westham Island DGPS Tower Removal BC.4
